name: Gianluigi Aponte
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2023); Forbes annual (2007-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Gianluigi Aponte and his wife Rafaela each own a 50% stake in MSC, the world's largest shipping line.
Gianluigi first met Rafaela on a trip to the Italian island of Capri in the 1960s, when he was a ship captain.
They entered the shipping industry together in 1970, when they purchased a ship with a $200,000 loan.
MSC also operates in holiday cruises (MSC Cruises), inland logistics (Medlog) and port operations (Terminal Investment Limited.)
Gianluigi is MSC's executive chairman; Rafaela is responsible for decorating ships for MSC Cruises and their son, Diego, is MSC's president.
forbes_facts: The second ship that the Apontes bought was named after Rafaela.
In December 2022, MSC bought Bolloré Africa Logistics, the African transport and logistics arm of the Bolloré Group, for $6 billion.

name: Abdulsamad Rabiu
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2014-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Abdulsamad Rabiu is the founder of BUA Group, a Nigerian conglomerate active in cement production, sugar refining and real estate.
In early January 2020, Rabiu merged his privately-owned Obu Cement company with listed firm Cement Co. of Northern Nigeria, which he controlled.
The combined firm, called BUA Cement Plc, trades on the Nigerian stock exchange; Rabiu owns 98.2% of it. He also owns 95% of publicly traded food conglomerate BUA Foods.
Rabiu, the son of a businessman, inherited land from his father.
He set up his own business in 1988 importing iron, steel and chemicals.
forbes_facts: His foundation, the Abdul Samad Rabiu Initiative, supports education, health and social development projects across Africa.

name: Scott Farquhar
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2015-2025); Hurun Global (2015-2026); Hurun Global U40 (2019-2020); Wikidata (2021); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Scott Farquhar is cofounder of collaboration software company Atlassian, based in Sydney, Australia.
He and CEO Mike Cannon-Brookes started the company soon after graduating from college, funding it with credit cards.
Atlassian's marquee customer list includes retailing giant Costco and American airline Delta.
Atlassian is a cofounder of Pledge 1%, which urges companies to donate at least 1% of equity, employee time or products to charity.
He stepped down as co-CEO in September 2024 to spend more time with his family and to pursue philanthropic activities. He continues as a board member and an advisor.
forbes_facts: In November 2025, he completed the Ironman triathlon which included a 26.2 mile marathon; a 2.4 mile swim and a 112-mile bicycle ride.

name: Eric Wittouck
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2019-2025); Hurun Global (2020-2026); Wikidata (2019)
forbes_bio: An heir to a Belgian sugar fortune, Eric Wittouck is a descendant of the family that founded Tiense Suicker.
Wittouck's net worth has expanded dramatically thanks to Invus, a New York private equity firm that mostly manages Wittouck's money.
Run by Ray Debbane, Invus has scored huge returns through investments like Cava and Weight Watchers.
Wittouck's decision to remain fully invested in Invus is one of the greatest investment decisions ever. His cousins mostly pulled their cash out 20 years ago.

name: Chase Coleman III
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2012-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Wikidata (2025)
forbes_bio: Chase Coleman III started out as a hedge fund investor, but his Tiger Global Management has evolved into a broader investment firm.
Tiger Global Management oversees $50 billion in assets. Its venture capital arm is now its biggest unit.
Prior to starting Tiger Global in 2001, Coleman worked for hedge fund legend Julian Robertson.
His longtime partner Scott Shleifer joined Tiger Global in 2002 and cofounded its venture business, which he led until the start of 2024.
Tiger Global's hedge fund fell more than 50% in 2022 after an impressive first two decades. It rebounded 20% in 2023 and 2024.
forbes_facts: Coleman is a descendant of Peter Stuyvesant, the last Dutch governor of New York.

name: Frederik Paulsen
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2014-2025); Hurun Global (2019-2026)
forbes_bio: Frederick Paulsen inherited small drugmaker Ferring Pharmaceuticals, founded by his father in 1950.
When he took over running the business in 1983, it generated $15 million in annual revenue.
Today the biotech outfit, which makes infertility, obstetrics, urology, gastroenterology and endocrinology drugs, has estimated sales of $2.2 billion.
Ferring employs more than 6,500 people and has subsidiaries in nearly 60 countries.
Board members include H?l?ne Ploix, former director of the IMF, and Alexandra, the Countess of Frederiksborg, a former Danish princess.
forbes_facts: Paulsen enjoys extreme adventure travel: he was the first person to cross the Bering Strait from Alaska to Russia in an ultralight aircraft.
Paulsen's father named the company Ferring after the name for inhabitants of F?hr, his native island off the coast of Germany.

name: Erich Wesjohann
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2021-2025); Hurun Global (2023-2026)
forbes_bio: Erich Wesjohann is the chairman and namesake of Germany-based EW Group, the world's largest poultry breeding and genetics company.
EW Group was founded in 1999, when Wesjohann and his brother Paul-Heinz decided to split up their family chicken company, originally dating to 1932.
In 2020, EW Group pulled in total revenue of $3.3 billion. Two U.S. poultry breeders Aviagen and Hubbard make up key assets in EW Group's portfolio.
The low-profile billionaire and his wife have transferred a portion of ownership in EW Group to other members of their family over the years.

name: Arkady Rotenberg
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2011-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: A friend of President Vladimir Putin, Arkady Rotenberg was once his judo sparring partner.
In the late 2000s Rotenberg became an owner of SGM Group and Mostotrest, now two of Russia's biggest construction contractors.
Both companies were targeted by EU sanctions in 2018 due to their participation in the construction of the Crimean bridge.
Rotenberg was also the target of U.S. and European sanctions in 2014.
In 2019 he sold SGM Group to a Gazprom subsidiary and agreed to transfer his shares of Mostotrest to a joint venture with state-owned Vnesheconombank.
forbes_facts: An ice hockey fan, Rotenberg apparently still plays with Putin and is chairman of the executive board of Russian Ice Hockey Federation.
Rotenberg holds an indirect stake in Sheremetyevo Airport, near Moscow.
In 2021 Rotenberg called himself the owner of huge complex of buildings on the Black Sea coast, which Russian oppositionist Alexei Navalny called "Putin's palace."

name: Yang Yunyun
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2024); Forbes annual (2021-2023); Hurun Global (2021-2024)
forbes_bio: Yang Yunyun is vice president in charge of risk management at China-headquartered retailer Miniso.
Yang's husband, fellow billionaire Ye Guofu, is chairman and CEO of Miniso.
Miniso has more than 4,200 stores in over 80 countries and regions.

name: Wang Jianlin
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2010-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Hurun China (2007-2026); Wikidata (2019)
forbes_bio: Wang Jianlin is the chairman of Dalian Wanda Group, which has investments in real estate, finance and movie theaters.
Dalian Wanda is one of the world's biggest commercial real estate developers with more than 500 plazas across China.
Once the richest man in Asia, Wang has been retreating in recent years, selling his Chinese hotel and tourism portfolio for over $9 billion in 2017.
The tycoon has also sold most of his stake in U.S. movie theater chain AMC and a stake in Spanish soccer club Atletico de Madrid.
In 2024, Wang ceded control of property management unit Zhuhai Wanda Commercial Management in an $8.3 billion deal, after failing to take it public on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange.
forbes_facts: Wang served in the Chinese military from 1970 to 1986 before turning around a government real estate venture and then going into business himself in 1989.
Wang previously served as a deputy to the 17th National Congress of the Communist Party of China.
